prompt: Produce one of each kind of method reference -- static (Integer::parseInt), unbound instance (String::trim), bound instance (list::size) and constructor (ArrayList::new) -- and let the tests prove the difference.
explanation: All four forms are shorthand for a lambda that does nothing but call one method. The subtle pair is String::trim versus list::size: the first names a type, so the single argument becomes the receiver, while the second names an object that is captured once, so later changes to that object are visible through the reference. ArrayList::new is a reference to a constructor, which is why every get() produces a fresh list instead of sharing one.
hints: Integer::parseInt matches Function<String, Integer> because parseInt takes a String and returns an int that autoboxes.
String::trim looks like it takes no argument, but as an unbound reference the Function's input becomes the string trim is called on.
sizeOf captures the parameter: the reference goes before the ::, so it reads list::size, not List::size.
